entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Assistants took our coats and showe..."
entries.dialogueText: Assistants took our coats and showed us into the meeting room where Symon, Edith, Gus and Mikail were waiting.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "As soon as I entered, their chatter..."
entries.dialogueText: As soon as I entered, their chatter stopped and they stood up. After a few pleasantries, everyone but Symon took their seats.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "He opened his briefcase, produced a..."
entries.dialogueText: He opened his briefcase, produced a folder and proceeded to go over some of the documents.

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Greetings, everyone. Welcome to th..."
entries.dialogueText: “Greetings, everyone. Welcome to the Ministry of Economy.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Without further ado...”"
entries.dialogueText: “Without further ado...”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“We are here today to discuss our e..."
entries.dialogueText: “We are here today to discuss our economic move towards nationalization.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“We are of course here today to dis..."
entries.dialogueText: “We are of course here today to discuss our economic shift towards privatization.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Mikail and Edith exchanged smiles."
entries.dialogueText: Mikail and Edith exchanged smiles.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Both Mikail and Edith had their arm..."
entries.dialogueText: Both Mikail and Edith had their arms crossed and frowns on their faces. They were listening intently.

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Before you arrived, certain indivi..."
entries.dialogueText: “Before you arrived, certain individuals in this room were voicing their opinion against a nationalization plan.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“But as I understand it, your decis..."
entries.dialogueText: “But as I understand it, your decision has already been made."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Mr. President.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Mr. President.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Which 'certain individuals' were t..."
entries.dialogueText: “Which 'certain individuals' were those?”
entries.menuText: “Which 'certain individuals' were those?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Yes. And you will respect my decis..."
entries.dialogueText: “Yes. And you will respect my decision whether you like it or not.”
entries.menuText: “Yes. And you will respect my decision whether you like it or not.”

entries.speaker: Mikail Aven
entries.title: Mikail Aven: "“Me and Edith's, Mr. President.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Me and Edith's, Mr. President.”

entries.speaker: Edith Agnoc
entries.title: Edith Agnoc: "“I am very much against a nationali..."
entries.dialogueText: “I am very much against a nationalization plan.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Too bad. Your opinion doesn't matt..."
entries.dialogueText: “Too bad. Your opinion doesn't matter.”
entries.menuText: “Too bad. Your opinion doesn't matter.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“And why is that?”"
entries.dialogueText: “And why is that?”
entries.menuText: “And why is that?”

entries.speaker: Edith Agnoc
entries.title: Edith Agnoc: "“But--”"
entries.dialogueText: “But--”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "One look from Symon stopped her. Bo..."
entries.dialogueText: One look from Symon stopped her. Both she and Mikail were restless in their seats.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“This is for the good of our countr..."
entries.dialogueText: “This is for the good of our country.”
entries.menuText: “This is for the good of our country.”

entries.speaker: Edith Agnoc
entries.title: Edith Agnoc: "“It's simple, really.”"
entries.dialogueText: “It's simple, really.”

entries.speaker: Edith Agnoc
entries.title: Edith Agnoc: "“Nationalization could provide an i..."
entries.dialogueText: “Nationalization could provide an improvement in terms of our economic development in the next year or two."

entries.speaker: Edith Agnoc
entries.title: Edith Agnoc: "“But in the long term, you are losi..."
entries.dialogueText: “But in the long term, you are losing people's trust. Without trust, there can be little trade. Especially if the government excessively nationalizes entire industries. Besides, it will cost us a proportional amount of government budget to nationalize.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“And you personally won't be able t..."
entries.dialogueText: “And you personally won't be able to profit. Isn't that right, Ms. Agnoc?”
entries.menuText: “And you personally won't be able to profit. Isn't that right, Ms. Agnoc?”

entries.speaker: Edith Agnoc
entries.title: Edith Agnoc: "“No. That is not my point.”"
entries.dialogueText: “No. That is not my point.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Are you saying that the state of S..."
entries.dialogueText: “Are you saying that the state of Sordland is untrustworthy?”
entries.menuText: “Are you saying that the state of Sordland is untrustworthy?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I've heard enough. You will accept..."
entries.dialogueText: “I've heard enough. You will accept my decision regardless.”
entries.menuText: “I've heard enough. You will accept my decision regardless.”

entries.speaker: Edith Agnoc
entries.title: Edith Agnoc: "“No. Of course it is trustworthy. T..."
entries.dialogueText: “No. Of course it is trustworthy. That is not my point.”

entries.speaker: Edith Agnoc
entries.title: Edith Agnoc: "“But, I-”"
entries.dialogueText: “But, I-”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“Let's not get ahead of ourselves,..."
entries.dialogueText: “Let's not get ahead of ourselves, shall we?”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“Mr. Holl. Please continue.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Mr. Holl. Please continue.”

entries.speaker: Edith Agnoc
entries.title: Edith Agnoc: "“I don't think so.”"
entries.dialogueText: “I don't think so.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Let's move on to how we can go abo..."
entries.dialogueText: “Let's move on to how we can go about implementing a nationalization plan.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Thank you, Mr. Galade.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Thank you, Mr. Galade.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Mr. President.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Mr. President.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "He handed me and everyone else in t..."
entries.dialogueText: He handed me and everyone else in the room two neat stacks of documents.

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Please turn to page 14.”"
entries.dialogueText: “Please turn to page 14.”

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I turned to page 14. The title was:..."
entries.dialogueText: I turned to page 14. The title was: Heart of Sordland.
entries.menuText: Turn to page 14.

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“As you can see on the document, th..."
entries.dialogueText: “As you can see on the document, the first corporation up for discussion is Heart of Sordland.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Led by fledgling CEO Marcel Koront..."
entries.dialogueText: “Led by fledgling CEO Marcel Koronti, HOS has recently observed a boost in their revenue. They control many media organisations across Sordland.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“It is possible to see their imprin..."
entries.dialogueText: “It is possible to see their imprint everywhere from newspaper stands to convenience stores. In fact, they own more than half of the media products in the country.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“We all know how much of an effect..."
entries.dialogueText: “We all know how much of an effect media has on politics.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“I must add that I myself am agains..."
entries.dialogueText: “I must add that I myself am against fully nationalizing any of these companies in principle.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: HOS Nationalization Hub

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“That is the reason I think if we a..."
entries.dialogueText: “That is the reason I think if we are to nationalize any corporation, HOS should be our target.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“However, we could partially move t..."
entries.dialogueText: “However, we could partially move the ownership of HOS to the state, gaining access to their income to help end the recession and provide for our citizens.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“I am inclined to agree with you fr..."
entries.dialogueText: “I am inclined to agree with you from a political perspective. However...”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“If we are going to nationalize HOS..."
entries.dialogueText: “If we are going to nationalize HOS, I think we should go all the way and fully move its ownership to the state.”

entries.dialogueText: “Theoretically. But we would still be making an enemy out of Marcel Koronti. He wouldn't be as powerful, of course, but I believe it's safer to move him off the chess board entirely."

entries.speaker: Symon Holl

entries.speaker: Symon Holl

entries.dialogueText: “It is led by current CEO and Lotherberg spokesman Walter Tusk. I believe all of us in the room are familiar with him in one way or another.”

entries.dialogueText: “What can I say? They have been widely successful since their founding. They have achieved renown not only in Sordland, but worldwide.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“I believe we shouldn't attempt to..."
entries.dialogueText: “I believe we shouldn't attempt to break something that is already working. I am against the nationalization of Bergia Steel in any capacity.”

entries.speaker: Mikail Aven
entries.title: Mikail Aven: "“Not to mention any amount of natio..."
entries.dialogueText: “Not to mention any amount of nationalization would be disastrous for both Bergia Steel and Sordland.”

entries.speaker: Mikail Aven
entries.title: Mikail Aven: "“Much of our steel trade is reliant..."
entries.dialogueText: “Much of our steel trade is reliant on their manufacturing capabilities. Any sudden change there would be like throwing a screwdriver in a working engine.”

entries.speaker: Edith Agnoc
entries.title: Edith Agnoc: "“No matter what, we should refrain..."
entries.dialogueText: “No matter what, we should refrain from nationalizing them. It could result in an economic crisis.”

entries.speaker: Lucian Galade
entries.title: Lucian Galade: "“I don't have so strong of an opini..."
entries.dialogueText: “I don't have so strong of an opinion. But I will say that nationalizing both Bergia Steel and HOS would be quite unwise."
